lesson_title: Classifying Triangles by Sides and Angles
hook_text: Seven bags filled. One bag could never be filled, and the label says why.
clip_script:
A Grade 8 is asked to sort a box of cardboard triangles for a Grade 4 teacher, who wants them in labelled bags by type. There are twenty-four triangles of different sizes and colours, and the Grade 4s have scribbled on some, so the sorting has to go by measurement, not appearance.

He sets up two tests. Sides: measure all three; three equal, equilateral; two equal, isosceles; none equal, scalene. Angles: check the largest corner against the corner of a sheet of paper; fits exactly, right-angled; smaller, acute; wider, obtuse. At the end he has seven bags and one empty label: equilateral right-angled. Nothing went in it, and nothing ever could, because three equal sides force three angles of 60.
visual_style: Cardboard triangles sliding into seven labelled bags; the eighth bag stays empty while 60, 60, 60 appears over an equilateral triangle
call_to_action: Open the full session to classify any triangle by its sides and its angles.
